background.fact: M2TS packages video, audio and additional streams for Blu-ray BDAV and AVCHD.
Its transport structure modifies MPEG-2 TS rather than prescribing one video codec.
Each source packet contains a 188-byte transport packet with four extra bytes.
Blu-ray permits MPEG-2, AVC and VC-1 picture streams in this wrapper.
AVCHD was announced by Sony and Panasonic in 2006.
The related MPEG transport-stream media type is video/mp2t; it is not unique to M2TS.

windows.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Reads MPEG transport streams; installed decoder support still matters.

mac.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Reads MPEG transport streams; installed decoder support still matters.

linux.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Reads MPEG transport streams; installed decoder support still matters.

problems.fact: Copying a stream alone omits its associated clip-information files and disc organization.
An M2TS extension does not identify which supported video decoder the recording needs.
Blu-ray content can have AACS protection even though M2TS itself supplies no encryption.

background.fact: MP2 means MPEG Audio Layer II and uses perceptual, lossy coding.
MPEG-1 Layer II is specified by ISO/IEC 11172-3.
ISO/IEC 13818-3 extends Layer II for MPEG-2.
MPEG-1 Layer II was finalized in 1992.
Layer II audio appears in digital broadcasting and Video CD production.
The Library of Congress lists audio/mpeg for MP2 files.

windows.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Its audio codec list includes MP2 decoding and encoding.

mac.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Its audio codec list includes MP2 decoding and encoding.

linux.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Its audio codec list includes MP2 decoding and encoding.

problems.fact: MP2 is Layer II audio, not a label for an MPEG-2 video recording.
Lossy MP2 coding omits sound information; decoding cannot recover that discarded material.
Surround playback needs a suitable multichannel speaker arrangement.

background.fact: MPEG-2 video is the picture coding defined by ISO/IEC 13818-2 and ITU-T H.262.
It combines block transforms with prediction between frames.
A video elementary stream includes pictures and decoding headers.
Audio and picture streams can be assembled into a program stream.
Transport streams can combine several programs.
The media type video/mpeg is registered for MPEG video.

windows.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Supports MPEG-2 video and MPEG program and transport streams.

mac.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Supports MPEG-2 video and MPEG program and transport streams.

linux.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Supports MPEG-2 video and MPEG program and transport streams.

problems.fact: A codec name alone does not identify whether the file uses an elementary, program or transport stream.
Predicted pictures depend on reference pictures, so not every encoded frame stands alone.
MPEG-2 compression can reduce detail; the encoder settings affect the visible result.

background.fact: ORF is the raw-picture extension used by Olympus and OM SYSTEM cameras.
Raw compatibility is tied to the camera model and application version.
OM-1 ORF support starts with Camera Raw 14.2 in Adobe's table.
OM Workspace develops raw images and provides white-balance and exposure adjustments.
Workspace records processing choices so an edit can return to its original settings.

windows.note: Check the minimum version for the exact camera.

mac.note: Check the minimum version for the exact camera.

linux.note: Lists ORF as a readable camera raw format; verify local delegates.

problems.fact: An older raw plug-in may lack the specific camera even when it understands other ORF files.
Some Workspace processing options cannot be used for every raw image.
High Res Shot raw processing requires at least 8 GB of memory in Workspace.

background.fact: An .rgb ending can identify an SGI image; Pillow registers that extension for its SGI reader.
The SGI header stores image width, height and channel count.
SGI images can use either direct samples or run-length compression.
Pillow's SGI reader recognizes grayscale, RGB and RGBA arrangements.
ImageMagick uses the separate RGB coder for raw sample streams that require size and depth parameters.
ImageMagick calls its SGI coder an Irix RGB image, distinguishing it from raw RGB.

windows.note: Use SGI for an SGI image; RGB means raw samples.
Python library with an SGI reader and writer.

mac.note: Use SGI for an SGI image; RGB means raw samples.
Python library with an SGI reader and writer.

linux.note: Use SGI for an SGI image; RGB means raw samples.
Python library with an SGI reader and writer.

problems.fact: Raw RGB and SGI are different data layouts despite the shared extension.
A raw sample stream needs its dimensions and bit depth supplied by the user.
Pillow can reject an SGI channel arrangement it does not implement.

background.fact: RealNetworks described RealMedia as a streaming container in a March 1998 Internet-Draft.
The historical draft describes playback from local storage or over a network.
RMFF uses tagged chunks whose identifiers have four characters.
A .RMF header identifies a RealMedia file.
Separate headers describe overall media properties and individual streams.

windows.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Lists RealMedia demuxing and muxing; individual codecs have separate support entries.

mac.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Lists RealMedia demuxing and muxing; individual codecs have separate support entries.

linux.note: Free playback utility using FFmpeg's libraries.
Lists RealMedia demuxing and muxing; individual codecs have separate support entries.

problems.fact: Container recognition does not establish support for every codec stored inside it.
A damaged or missing initial .RMF header prevents normal file identification.
An old RM specification is work in progress, so its version-specific structures should not be treated as a current universal guarantee.

background.fact: ZSoft created PCX for its PC Paintbrush graphics program.
The format emerged for MS-DOS in the 1984–1985 period.
PCX is a raster image format using run-length encoding.
A PCX begins with a 128-byte header.
Some PCX variants carry an additional palette at the end of the file.
A DCX document groups PCX pictures, commonly for fax applications.

windows.note: Reads and writes PCX in its documented supported modes.

mac.note: Reads and writes PCX in its documented supported modes.

linux.note: Reads and writes PCX in its documented supported modes.

problems.fact: Applications may omit support for this older format even when they open newer bitmap formats.
Reading a DCX as though it were one PCX loses the document's multiple-image structure.
Pillow's PCX writer accepts monochrome, grayscale, palette and RGB data, rather than arbitrary channel arrangements.

background.fact: PES contains embroidery data used by Brother's PE-DESIGN workflow.
PE-DESIGN 11 can display PES designs as Explorer thumbnails in its full edition.
PES files saved by PE-DESIGN 11 may be larger because they contain more design information.
Ink/Stitch can both import PES and export PES.
Brother Artspira accepts PES embroidery files on iOS and Android.

windows.note: Free embroidery extension with PES import and export.
Brother application; the trial has restricted features.

mac.note: PES import and export through its Inkscape extension.

linux.note: PES import and export through its Inkscape extension.

mobile.note: Accepts PES uploads on iOS and Android.

problems.fact: A design may exceed a machine's USB-connected storage capacity; Brother suggests a USB flash drive where supported.
PES export cannot contain more than 255 color changes according to Ink/Stitch's troubleshooting documentation.
The PE-DESIGN 11 trial lacks the PES thumbnail integration included in the full program.

background.fact: EPUB packages digital publications and their resources in one container.
Its publication content can include HTML, CSS and SVG.
An EPUB container uses ZIP packaging.
The publication's reading sequence is described by its spine.
The EPUB media type is application/epub+zip.
EPUB 3.3 is maintained as a W3C Recommendation.

windows.note: Free reader with EPUB navigation and bookmarks.
Free reader supporting EPUB and EPUB 3.

mac.note: Free reader with EPUB navigation and bookmarks.
Free reader supporting EPUB and EPUB 3.

linux.note: Free Linux reader for EPUB publications.
Launch from the desktop menu or ebook-viewer.

web.note: Reads uploaded EPUB publications through a signed-in account.

mobile.note: Imports EPUB files from device storage.
Available for mobile devices and supports EPUB.

problems.fact: An ACSM purchase file is a download instruction, not the EPUB itself; Digital Editions retrieves the book.
DRM can keep calibre from opening a purchased EPUB even though it can store and transfer it.
A converted EPUB may need a separate validity check before submission to a store.
